subject.title: fix(sessions): guard sessions.create fork against cross-plugin ownership bypass

question: Should plugin runtimes be categorically barred from using ownerless user sessions as parents, matching the existing delete ownership rule?
rationale: The complete repair depends on confirming that ownerless sessions are outside every plugin runtime’s authority; this is a sensitive-data boundary even though the existing delete behavior strongly supports exact equality.

options.title: Require exact owner equality
options.body: Reject ownerless and differently owned parents for every plugin-runtime parent-session operation.

options.title: Permit ownerless parents
options.body: Allow plugins to use user-owned sessions as parents and explicitly document and test that broader read and linking authority.

recommendation.title: Require exact owner equality
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless and differently owned parents for every plugin-runtime parent-session operation.

likelyOwner.reason: Tyler is the strongest feature-history owner for the session parent-linkage and management behavior affected by this boundary.
